chapter_title: Polar Covalent Bonds; Acids and Bases

questions.chapter_title: Polar Covalent Bonds; Acids and Bases
questions.question: What is the expected major product when Acetic acid (CH3COOH) is treated with Sodium hydroxide (NaOH)?
questions.explanation: Treating Acetic acid (CH3COOH) with Sodium hydroxide (NaOH) yields Sodium acetate (CH3COONa) + H2O. Rationale: Hydroxide abstracts the acidic carboxyl proton, producing the resonance-stabilized acetate anion.

questions.chapter_title: Polar Covalent Bonds; Acids and Bases
questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of Methylamine (CH3NH2) into Methylammonium chloride (CH3NH3+ Cl-)?
questions.explanation: To convert Methylamine (CH3NH2) into Methylammonium chloride (CH3NH3+ Cl-), the appropriate reagent is Hydrochloric acid (HCl). Rationale: The basic nitrogen lone pair is protonated by strong acid to yield an alkylammonium salt.

questions.chapter_title: Polar Covalent Bonds; Acids and Bases
questions.question: What is the expected major product when Acetic acid (pKa 4.75) is treated with Sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO3)?

options.label: C
options.text: Sodium acetate + Carbonic acid (H2CO3 -> CO2 + H2O)

questions.correct_answer: Sodium acetate + Carbonic acid (H2CO3 -> CO2 + H2O)
questions.explanation: Treating Acetic acid (pKa 4.75) with Sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO3) yields Sodium acetate + Carbonic acid (H2CO3 -> CO2 + H2O). Rationale: Acetic acid is stronger than carbonic acid (pKa 6.35), driving the equilibrium toward CO2 release.

questions.chapter_title: Polar Covalent Bonds; Acids and Bases
questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of Phenol (C6H5OH) into Sodium phenoxide (C6H5ONa) + H2O?
questions.explanation: To convert Phenol (C6H5OH) into Sodium phenoxide (C6H5ONa) + H2O, the appropriate reagent is Aqueous sodium hydroxide (NaOH). Rationale: Phenol is sufficiently acidic (pKa 10) to be fully deprotonated by hydroxide into resonance-stabilized phenoxide.

questions.chapter_title: Polar Covalent Bonds; Acids and Bases
questions.question: What is the expected major product when Acetylene (HC≡CH) is treated with Sodium amide (NaNH2) in liquid NH3?

options.label: B
options.text: Sodium acetate + Carbonic acid (H2CO3 -> CO2 + H2O)

questions.explanation: Treating Acetylene (HC≡CH) with Sodium amide (NaNH2) in liquid NH3 yields Sodium acetylide (HC≡C- Na+) + NH3. Rationale: The strong base amide (pKa conjugate NH3 = 38) deprotonates the sp-hybridized terminal alkyne (pKa 25).

questions.chapter_title: Polar Covalent Bonds; Acids and Bases
questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of Boron trifluoride (BF3) into BF3•OEt2 complex?
questions.explanation: To convert Boron trifluoride (BF3) into BF3•OEt2 complex, the appropriate reagent is Diethyl ether ((C2H5)2O). Rationale: The ether oxygen donates an electron pair into boron's empty 2p orbital.

questions.chapter_title: Polar Covalent Bonds; Acids and Bases
questions.question: Which starting material will react with Concentrated sulfuric acid (H2SO4) to yield Ethyloxonium hydrogen sulfate (CH3CH2OH2+ HSO4-) as the major product?
questions.explanation: Ethanol (CH3CH2OH) reacts with Concentrated sulfuric acid (H2SO4) to yield Ethyloxonium hydrogen sulfate (CH3CH2OH2+ HSO4-). Rationale: Strong sulfuric acid protonates the weakly basic alcohol hydroxyl group into an oxonium ion.

questions.chapter_title: Polar Covalent Bonds; Acids and Bases
questions.question: What is the expected major product when Acetone (CH3COCH3) is treated with Sodium hydride (NaH)?

options.label: A
options.text: Sodium acetate + Carbonic acid (H2CO3 -> CO2 + H2O)

questions.explanation: Treating Acetone (CH3COCH3) with Sodium hydride (NaH) yields Sodium acetone enolate + H2 gas. Rationale: Hydride irreversibly abstracts an acidic alpha-proton (pKa 19.3), releasing hydrogen gas.

questions.chapter_title: Polar Covalent Bonds; Acids and Bases
questions.question: Which starting material will react with Concentrated HCl (aq) to yield Benzoic acid precipitate (C6H5COOH) + NaCl as the major product?
questions.explanation: Sodium benzoate (C6H5COONa) reacts with Concentrated HCl (aq) to yield Benzoic acid precipitate (C6H5COOH) + NaCl. Rationale: Protonation converts the water-soluble carboxylate salt into insoluble neutral benzoic acid.

questions.chapter_title: Polar Covalent Bonds; Acids and Bases
questions.question: What is the expected major product when Octylamine in diethyl ether is treated with 1 M Aqueous hydrochloric acid?
questions.explanation: Treating Octylamine in diethyl ether with 1 M Aqueous hydrochloric acid yields Octylammonium chloride in aqueous layer. Rationale: Protonation converts the neutral lipophilic amine into a water-soluble ammonium cation.
